title: Knowledge check: Understanding the Node.js Event Loop

questions.prompt: In Understanding the Node.js Event Loop, which statement best describes Event-driven server behavior?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Understanding the Node.js Event Loop: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Connect this syllabus point to Understanding the Node.js Event Loop: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Understanding the Node.js Event Loop?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.
questions.answer_key: Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.

questions.prompt: A change related to Understanding the Node.js Event Loop appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
